input.brief: 四渡赤水：为什么这样走。手机优先的真实历史互动叙事，河流、山地与四段动态行军路线为核心。

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Film title, bottom edge
hero.blueprint: One photograph fills the viewport at 100vw by 100svh, `object-fit: cover`, with its subject in the upper two-thirds and a calmer, darker zone along the bottom. The name is one condensed uppercase word, or a short name in a high-contrast serif, set at clamp(150px, 17.5vw, 290px) and sized to span the full width between 32px margins. It is centred and anchored so its baseline sits 34px above the bottom edge, covering roughly the lowest quarter of the frame. A soft neutral dark scrim lies under that bottom band only, about 40% of the height; the rest of the image is untouched. Directly above the name's left end, on the same margin, sits the supporting sentence at 16px on two short lines. Directly above its right end, right-aligned, sits the single action as a small paper-coloured rectangular button. The top edge carries a small emblem or wordmark at the left margin and up to five text links at 15px grouped at the right, all in white. The central half of the screen belongs to the view.
hero.mobile: The photograph is re-cropped to portrait with `object-position` on its subject and fills 100svh. The name stays on the bottom edge at 22vw on one line, or two lines at 20vw beyond eight characters, 20px above the edge. The supporting sentence sits above the name's left end at 15px. The action button moves to the top-right corner and the links collapse to a menu word beside the emblem.
hero.headline: The name of the place: one word of up to about 12 characters at 17.5vw, or two words stacked on a phone.

motion.name: Slow crossfade
motion.description: The principal photograph quietly changes: three or four images of the same framing crossfade over about 1.6 seconds, holding five to six seconds each, or the fixed image changes when its matching section arrives. It should feel like light shifting in a room. Pause when the tab is hidden; under reduced motion show only the first image.

sections.name: Right-half paragraph, lone photo
sections.blueprint: No heading. On a 12-column grid with 5vw margins, one statement paragraph of 45–70 words occupies columns 7–12 only, set at clamp(24px, 2.2vw, 34px) with leading 1.25 and a first-line indent of 3em. Its top edge sits 18vh below the section top. Columns 1–6 stay empty except for a single square photograph, 20vw wide, in columns 1–3, placed so its top aligns with the paragraph's last line and it hangs below the text by most of its height. A five-line note at 14px, 180px wide, sits in columns 1–2, 96px beneath the photograph. Section padding is 160px top and bottom. Nothing is centred: the paragraph's left edge is the midpoint of the page, and later text blocks on the page may reuse that line. Holds one paragraph, one photograph and one note.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 22px, full width with 20px margins and no indent. The photograph follows at 62% width, pushed to the right margin, in a 4:5 crop instead of square. The small note sits to its left, bottom-aligned with the photograph, in the remaining 30% of the width.

sections.name: Accordion of tinted panels
sections.blueprint: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion. Introduction: the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), in columns 1–5; one paragraph at 18px in columns 7–11. 64px below, a flex row across columns 1–12, 520px tall, of four to six panels with no gaps. The open stage is a panel taking about 58% of the width; the rest are vertical slivers sharing what remains. Order is carried by colour: the first stage is the darkest tone of one hue and each later stage is a lighter flat tint of it, so the row reads dark to light from left to right. A sliver shows only its stage name, rotated 90 degrees and reading upward, at 20px bold, anchored to its bottom-left. The open panel shows the name at 40px top-left, a 36ch paragraph at 18px bottom-left and, optionally, one photograph in its right half. Clicking a sliver opens it (flex-basis transition, 450ms).
sections.mobile: The accordion turns vertical: stages stack at full width as bars 64px tall in the same dark-to-light order, names set horizontally at 18px. The open stage expands to its content height with the paragraph at 17px. The first stage is open by default.

sections.name: Portrait as drop cap
sections.blueprint: No heading. One biography paragraph of 50–80 words is set large at clamp(24px, 2.5vw, 38px), regular weight, leading 1.2, across columns 3–12 of the grid. A square portrait is floated at the paragraph's start with `float: left`: its side equals three lines of text (3.6em), with 0.5em of space to its right, so the first three lines wrap beside it and the fourth returns to the paragraph's left edge, like a drop capital. Square corners. The person's name, the first words of the paragraph, is in full ink; the rest may be in a softer ink with linked names in full ink and underlined. A second paragraph follows after one blank line in the soft ink at the same size. Columns 1–2 hold three short facts (place, since when, how to reach) at 14px, top-aligned with the portrait. Section padding 140px.
sections.mobile: Text at 22px with leading 1.25, full width. The portrait keeps its float but grows to four lines tall, about 110px square. The three facts move below the second paragraph as a single row of three small blocks at 13px.

sections.name: Name first, places under it
sections.blueprint: The wordmark opens the footer instead of closing it. On a full-bleed field in the page's inverse or final chapter colour, the name spans the full content width as the first thing, its cap line pushed 8% above the footer's top edge so the tops of the letters are sliced off by the section (`overflow: hidden` and a negative top margin in `em`). 72px beneath, a two-part row: columns 1–5 list the places or ways to reach the studio (cities, or email and telephone), one per line at 32–36px in the accent ink, each a link; columns 7–12 hold three columns of small links at 15px, top-aligned with the first place. A final row 96px lower carries the legal line at the left and a back-to-top text link at the right, both 13px. The field is about 90svh tall, and nothing sits between the wordmark and the row but space.
sections.mobile: The sliced wordmark stays at the top, fitted to the width. Places follow as a list at 26px, then the link columns two across at 15px. Legal line and back-to-top link share the last row at 12px, at opposite margins.

references.name: Produx Design
references.idea: The wordmark is the hero, and the showreel image assembles itself from scattered square fragments as you scroll.
references.hero: Near-black field with 80px side margins. The wordmark, in a wide, light-weight uppercase sans with a slashed O, runs margin to margin (about 89% of the width) with a cap height near 20% of the viewport, starting 9% from the top. A large empty gap follows. In the lower half a two-line statement at 5.1vw sits flush left; opposite it, bottom-aligned to the statement and flush to the right margin, is a three-line paragraph in small monospace about a quarter of the width. No nav bar, button or image in the first viewport; the bottom quarter is empty.
references.type: At Aero in light-to-medium weight for the wordmark, the 74px statement and project titles; DM Mono for the hero paragraph, bracketed nav items and uppercase project blurbs at about 11px. Three sizes; the statement is roughly five times the mono text.
references.colour: #0e0e0e #e4e4e4 #545e54 #303930 #6f8f3a — Near-black page with off-white type and no accent colour. Colour arrives only through imagery: moss green and sage in the showreel render, then each case-study thumbnail brings its own palette.
references.imagery: A 3D render of a moss-covered boulder on a sage background, first broken into scattered square tiles, then whole as a 16:9 inset. Work thumbnails are square-cornered stills and video in mixed ratios, including one vivid orange-violet gradient card.
references.layout: 80px margins. After the hero, a small logo top-left and four bracketed mono links spread across the right half. Hero is all type, the next three screens are a pinned image assembly, then a work grid with unequal column widths and mono captions under each thumbnail.

sections.description: Pinned showreel reveal on black. Eight to ten small square tiles, 60 to 100px, each a different crop of the same image, float scattered around the centre at different depths, some blurred. As scroll advances they multiply, enlarge and lock together until they form one 16:9 image inset at about 70% of viewport width, with the wordmark centred on it in white and tiny captions overlaid at left and lower right.

Two unequal columns on black, roughly 52% and 30% of the width with a wide gutter. Each item is a square-cornered thumbnail with a row of small rectangular mono tags along its bottom edge; beneath it a small square bullet, the project name in the sans at about 16px and a two-line uppercase mono blurb. The next item breaks the grid: a single thumbnail centred at about 75% width.

steal: Run the wordmark margin to margin in a light weight rather than a heavy one; thin strokes at huge size read as assured instead of loud.
Pair one large sans statement with a tiny monospace paragraph bottom-aligned on the opposite margin and leave the middle of the row empty.
Introduce the hero image as scattered square crops of itself that converge into the full frame on scroll.
references.media: The fold has no media at all; the first picture is the 40s showreel, which arrives on the second screen as scattered square tiles at different depths that converge into an inset 16:9 frame, then fills 56-96% of each screen until it is full-bleed at about 4850px. Below: a staggered two-column mosaic with a centred wide interlude, a logo strip bleeding off both edges, and a pinned 3D stone centre-right with the statement docked bottom-left; zero radius everywhere.
references.motion: Black at 400ms, then wordmark letters rise one by one out of a baseline mask, tagline words rise in masked lines and the small blurb types itself out, settled by about 2.2s. Lenis drives a sticky, scrubbed hero in which tiles fly in from depth, blurred to sharp, assemble the frame and scale it to full bleed, then headings resolve through a pixel-slice glitch, work frames reveal by inset clip, the manifesto colours word by word and the closing stone grows moss as the ground turns from black to moss green, all as per-frame script (44,246 style mutations) with no GSAP exposed.

references.name: House of Honey
references.idea: A block-heavy wordmark pierced by a hairline script: the bold-against-delicate contrast is repeated at every scale, with giant pink script behind quiet serif statements.
references.hero: Top 42% is a flat blush-pink band; the bottom 58% is a full-bleed photograph of a bright living room, arched window on the centre axis, butting against the band with no margin. A tiny nav row sits at the very top with 8px side margins: block logo glyph and five links left, contact link with a small square arrow box far right. The wordmark fills the width edge to edge: two words in ultra-black extended caps, about 120px cap height, dark aubergine, with a hairline script 'of' 230px tall between them, overshooting above and below. Directly beneath, two two-line serif uppercase taglines at 31px, one flush left, one flush right.
references.type: Wordmark in ultra-black extended caps; statements in noeText serif, uppercase, 31–40px, tight tracking; nav and captions in neueHaasGrotesk around 14px; 'canora' hairline script for the connecting word and for cropped background words at 37vw. Three contrasting voices, each with one job.
references.colour: #edccbe #331917 #0e0e0e #f26fcb #ffffff — Blush pink and dark aubergine-brown alternate as full fields and as each other's text colour. Hot pink appears only in the oversized script and a 2px divider. Photographs bring saturated colour.
references.imagery: Editorial interior photography, saturated and daylight-lit. Hero is a full-bleed landscape crop; projects are portrait crops about 5:6 in a three-column grid with 4px gutters and square corners.
references.layout: Edge-to-edge with 8px outer margins. Typographic sections (small centred label, serif statement, cropped giant script) alternate with a three-column image grid. Blush and brown fields swap each section; hairline link rows close blocks. The footer is a full-width logo glyph.

sections.description: Dark aubergine field under the hero photo, separated by a 2px hot-pink line. A small sans label centred, then a three-line centred serif uppercase statement at about 31px in blush, 45% of the width. Behind it a hot-pink script phrase set near 37vw runs off both sides and is cut by the section's bottom edge, its ascenders rising into the statement. A smaller serif line follows.

Title card before the project grid. Blush field, nearly empty screen. A small label and a one-line serif uppercase heading about 40px sit centred at 55% height. The giant pink script returns, cropped by the bottom edge so only its top half shows and running off both sides.

Three columns edge to edge with 4px gutters and 8px outer margins. Portrait photos about 500×580px, square corners. Under each: an uppercase sans title at 14px and a grey line of GPS coordinates. Two rows, then a full-width hairline row with a text link left and a small square arrow box at the far right.

Brown field. The logo glyph is enlarged to full width and about a third of the screen: blush rectangles and quarter-circle arcs with 4px gaps, forming an abstract monogram. Below: four columns of small links, a hairline, two addresses in the first two columns, another hairline, then copyright left and a small blush button right.

steal: Set a wordmark edge to edge in ultra-heavy extended caps and thread a hairline script connecting word through it that overshoots the cap height both ways.
Use an oversized script word in one hot accent colour as a cropped background layer behind small, calm serif statements.
Split a tagline into two halves, flush left and flush right on the same baseline under the wordmark, instead of centring it.
references.media: The lower 58% of the fold is a full-bleed interior photograph that continues for one full viewport as a five-image crossfading slideshow with a pink progress line on its bottom edge. Below: a three-up grid of 4:5 project tiles with 8px gutters sliding over a giant script marquee, a full-bleed tinted feature photograph with its title docked bottom-left, a full-bleed photograph with an inset colour card, and one giant cropped letterform as the footer's picture, the photographs oversized to 110-170% of their frames for drift and no video anywhere.
references.motion: There is no visible preloader and the page is whole at 400ms; under Lenis, blocks rise 8px and fade in over 800ms ease-out at 0-260ms staggers (39 WAAPI calls), slideshow crossfades take 600ms cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.25,1), the oversized photographs drift, and script marquees run on CSS time (90-122s per pair). Page changes use a 1s view transition on the same curve; nothing pins, and there is one reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Trevor Noah
references.idea: The comedian as a paper cut-out sticker: his head is torn open and the things he makes (stand-up, books, video) spill out and become the navigation.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught a blank navy frame before the canvas painted; the next frame and the mobile shot show the scene. A deep navy field. The name runs across the top in bold pink grotesk on one line, sized to nearly touch both edges. Centred below is a photographic cut-out of the face with a thick white sticker outline and a torn top edge, from which glossy 3D objects (microphone, book, video player, brain, heart) erupt. Circular arrow buttons sit at the left and right edges; a torn-paper white label beneath the face names the current category. A hairline, a text ticker and a pink pill close the bottom.
references.type: Die Grotesk D bold for the wordmark (361px in the digest), Die Grotesk C for everything else with body near 19px. Tight tracking, title case. Statements run at about 4vw and emphasise words by switching them to pink, never by changing weight or face.
references.colour: #1d2440 #f78fb3 #f6f7ee #2b2b2b — One navy field for the entire page. Pink marks the wordmark, emphasised words and one pill; cream-white fills buttons and paper shapes. Photos bring the only other colour.
references.imagery: Photo cut-outs of the face with thick white die-cut outlines and torn edges, toy-like 3D objects, and small stage photos shaped as peeling stickers or rounded tiles, tilted a few degrees and loosely clustered.
references.layout: Centred, one idea per screen on an unbroken navy ground: statement, section title with drifting objects, a lone pill button. The fixed header has the pink name left and two cream pills right. Elements enter from the edges and overlap instead of sitting in columns.

sections.description: A centred four-line statement in white at about 4vw, the lines stepped and ragged instead of squared off, with one long word in pink on the first line. It occupies the lower half of the viewport while the upper half stays empty navy, and appears to build line by line.

A two-line centred title, first line white and second pink, at about 2.5vw. Beneath it a loose cluster of tilted objects rises from the bottom edge: a 3D video-player tile in the middle, small rounded photo tiles and a 3D microphone to its left, all overlapping. On the next screen the objects have drifted upward past a single cream pill button centred in empty space.

Split footer. Left half: a second, larger cut-out of the face, tilted and cropped by the left and bottom edges, with a small white speech bubble above it. Right half: a five-row menu, each row a tiny index number at left and a bold label at about 2.5vw, separated by hairlines. Legal text is tiny along the bottom.

steal: Cut the subject out of a photo with a thick white sticker border and a torn edge so photography behaves like illustration.
Emphasise words in a statement by colour alone (pink within white) while keeping one face and one weight.
Turn the footer into a large numbered menu beside a cropped portrait whose speech bubble addresses the departing visitor.
references.media: Media covers essentially the whole first screen: a fixed WebGL layer behind everything, a photographic cut-out of the face with a torn top taking about a third of the width and the bottom two thirds of the height, props bursting out of it over the wordmark. Later the props re-form into a collage of tilted sticker photos round a 3D object and a stack of books, torn-paper strips mark the colour changes, and a giant cropped portrait peeks from the footer corner, every photo an alpha cut-out with an 8-10px white sticker outline and no video anywhere.
references.motion: A load of about 7.3s plays as a large counter to 100, the intact face sticker, the crown tearing away, props spilling out and the name last, and Lenis then drives the fixed WebGL stage as the props fly down and re-form per chapter, the ground changing navy, charcoal, navy at torn-paper dividers. Headline lines rise from translateY(120%) through a clip-path over 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1) and stickers pop in from scale 0 on an overshoot curve the house layer does not use, while 11 reduced-motion rules zero every duration.
